description: Starts the workflow manually when the user clicks execute. Used for testing or manually-run workflows.
Starts the workflow on a time-based schedule such as every hour, day, or via a cron expression.
Starts the workflow when an HTTP request is received from an external service. Common entry point for integrations.
Sends an HTTP request to any API or URL and returns the response. Used to call external services not covered by dedicated nodes.
Adds, edits, or removes fields on the incoming data items. Used to reshape or prepare data before the next step.
Routes items down one of two branches based on a true/false condition. Used for conditional logic.
Routes items down multiple branches based on matching rules or an expression. Used for multi-way conditional routing.
Combines data from two or more incoming branches into a single output, by appending, matching, or waiting for all inputs.
Runs custom JavaScript or Python code on the incoming items for advanced data transformation not possible with standard nodes.
Keeps only the items that match a given condition and discards the rest.
Processes incoming items in smaller batches or one at a time, useful for rate-limited APIs or large datasets.
Sends messages, uploads files, or manages channels in Slack.
Sends, reads, or searches emails through a Gmail account.
Reads, appends, or updates rows in a Google Sheets spreadsheet.
Runs queries or inserts/updates rows in a PostgreSQL database.
Reads, creates, or updates records in an Airtable base.
Creates or updates pages and database entries in Notion.
Sends prompts to an OpenAI model for text generation, classification, or summarization.
Starts a separate workflow whenever another workflow throws an error, used for alerting or cleanup.
Passes data through unchanged. Used as a placeholder or a merge point for readability.
Pauses the workflow execution for a set time or until a webhook is called, then resumes.
Sends a custom HTTP response back to the caller of a webhook trigger, ending that execution branch.
Combines multiple items into a single item, for example summing values or collecting a list of fields.
Formats, parses, or performs calculations on date and time values.
Sends or receives messages through a Telegram bot.
